cards.front: Name the four Vedas in order and the one considered oldest.
cards.back: Rigveda (oldest, hymns), Samaveda (melodies), Yajurveda (rituals), Atharvaveda (spells & charms). The Rigveda has 1,028 hymns in 10 mandalas.

cards.front: Which Harappan site shows evidence of a dockyard?
cards.back: Lothal (Gujarat) — a tidal dockyard connected to the Gulf of Khambhat, evidence of maritime trade. Other key sites: Dholavira (water management), Kalibangan (ploughed field).

cards.front: Who introduced the Iqta system in India and what was it?
cards.back: Iltutmish institutionalised the Iqta system — land revenue assignments to officers (iqtadars/muqtis) in lieu of salary, transferable and non-hereditary in principle.

cards.front: What were the key features of Akbar's Mansabdari system?
cards.back: Rank-based (zat = personal status/salary; sawar = cavalry to maintain), directly appointed/promoted/dismissed by the Emperor, non-hereditary, paid in cash or jagir.

cards.front: What was the Doctrine of Lapse and who applied it aggressively?
cards.back: Annexation policy of Lord Dalhousie (1848–56): states of rulers dying without a natural male heir 'lapsed' to the Company. Satara (1848), Jhansi (1853), Nagpur (1854) annexed.

cards.front: Why was the Partition of Bengal (1905) carried out and when was it annulled?
cards.back: Officially for administrative convenience; really to divide Hindus and Muslims. Sparked the Swadeshi & Boycott movement. Annulled in 1911 (capital shifted to Delhi).

cards.front: What were the three demands of Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha context and its significance?
cards.back: Champaran (1917, Bihar) — against the tinkathia system forcing indigo cultivation on 3/20th of land. Gandhi's first Civil Disobedience in India; showed the power of Satyagraha.

cards.front: Differentiate: Non-Cooperation Movement vs Civil Disobedience Movement (aims & methods).
cards.back: NCM (1920–22): withdraw cooperation (titles, schools, courts, foreign cloth); called off after Chauri Chaura. CDM (1930–34): actively break laws — began with Dandi Salt March (12 Mar 1930).

cards.front: Match the classical dance to its state: Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Sattriya.
cards.back: Kathakali — Kerala; Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh; Odissi — Odisha; Sattriya — Assam (introduced by Srimanta Sankardev, recognised in 2000).

cards.front: Which Ashokan edict mentions the Kalinga War and his change of heart?
cards.back: Major Rock Edict XIII — describes the Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE), Ashoka's remorse, and his turn to Dhamma vijaya (conquest by righteousness) over military conquest.
